item.title: AI-related cyber risks drive growing insurance interest among UK SMEs, says Brit
item.description: According to Brit, these developments are having a direct bearing on demand for insurance, with more than two-thirds of SMEs reporting that AI-related risks have strengthened their interest in obtaining cyber protection. Concerns surrounding artificial intelligence and the increasing complexity of cyber attacks are influencing insurance decisions among UK small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), according to research published by Brit Insurance, a specialty insurance and reinsurance provider operating in the Lloyd’s market. The insurer’s findings indicate that 68% of SMEs are now more inclined to purchase cyber insurance because of risks associated with AI.

item.title: Kalshi Loses Bid to Prevent Maryland From Policing Prediction Market
item.description: A US appeals court on Tuesday ruled that Kalshi cannot prevent Maryland gaming regulators from pursuing enforcement actions against the prediction market operator for allowing users to place financial bets on sports without a license. Kalshi in a statement said Tuesday’s decision “demonstrates there is no unified coherent legal argument against prediction markets.” New Jersey Takes Fight Over Kalshi’s Prediction Market to US Supreme Court Jeremy Baker, the acting director of the Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Commission, in a statement welcomed the ruling, saying it “affirmed the state’s ability to regulate what is clearly sports wagering.” Kalshi and similar companies allow users to trade on the outcomes of events such as sports and elections. The 2-1 decision by the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals deepens a split among federal appeals courts over whether state gaming regulators have the power to police prediction markets operated by Kalshi and competing platforms.

item.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
item.description: The next two largest fundraisers on our list for this year are focused on automating more employer tasks. So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. As you can see, it’s a varied list, with a commonly shared theme of bringing more automation to hiring, HR and payroll tasks.

item.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
item.description: To put this in perspective: If the blue economy were a country, it would be the world’s fifth largest. And as the world turns back to the sea to face increasingly critical challenges, from geopolitical instability to rising energy prices and climate resilience, the blue economy is set to become even more central. The “blue economy,” which encompasses industries built around oceans and coasts — from shipping and fisheries to offshore energy and marine biotechnology — is one of the largest, yet least visible, engines of the global economy.

item.title: Allied World raises target to $375m for 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 catastrophe bond
item.description: Now, we’re told that Allied World is looking for even more protection from its latest catastrophe bond, with the target size raised to now seek $375 million of retrocession from the issuance of three tranches of 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 notes. Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC) is aiming to upsize its new catastrophe bond sponsorship to provide $375 million of protection, while also targeting strong execution as the price guidance has been lowered for all three tranches of 2001 CAT Re Ltd. Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC), the global insurance and reinsurance company that is part of the Fairfax Financial group, returned to the catastrophe bond market for a renewal and expansion of its protection earlier this month.

item.title: Capital markets signal resilience for Lloyd’s despite rate softening narratives: ICMR
item.description: As rate softening continues to take shape across the Lloyd’s market, Insurance Capital Markets Research (ICMR) has pointed to the capital markets as proof that investors see a more resilient outlook and considerable upside potential ahead. Moreover, Insurance Capital Markets Research also emphasises that while direct data on rate softening is too inconsistent and client-specific to measure accurately, it instead relies on the broader, aggregate perspective of the capital markets to gauge its overall impact. However, while the new launches demonstrate “sustained capital appetite”, ICMR stressed that they could potentially add underwriting capacity into classes already facing downward rate pressure, widening the gap between top-quartile cycle managers and those chasing volume.

item.title: Frequent acquirers better placed to achieve insurance M&A goals: Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY
item.description: Insurance companies with established acquisition programmes may be more successful at securing the anticipated benefits of mergers and acquisitions (M&A), according to a joint study by Oxbow Partners, a specialist insurance management consultancy, and InsurTech NY, an organisation supporting connections between insurers, technology businesses and investors. Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY assessed 333 publicly listed insurance carriers and gathered perspectives from industry executives and transaction specialists with experience of significant insurance deals. Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY suggest that decisions concerning how businesses will operate together should form part of the initial assessment of a potential acquisition.

item.title: Tokio Marine’s international insurance profit rises 13% to JPY 266.8bn in Q2’26
item.description: Tokio Marine’s international business has reported a total insurance profit of JPY 266.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 12.7% from JPY 236.8 billion in the same period a year earlier. The increase in profit was driven by strong underwriting, primarily in North America, which generated an insurance profit of JPY 230.9 billion, a 20.2% increase from JPY 192 billion a year earlier. LATAM also recorded significant growth, with insurance profit increasing 99.4% to JPY 21.5 billion from JPY 10.7 billion.

item.title: Canopius Reinsurance adopts ACORD Solutions Group’s ADEPT Platform in Bermuda
item.description: Canopius Reinsurance Limited has introduced the ADEPT digital data exchange platform in Bermuda to manage the transfer of accounting, claims and financial settlement information with its broker partners, according to ACORD Solutions Group, a provider of digital data exchange and technology solutions for the global insurance industry. We are pleased to support the continued rollout of ADEPT in Bermuda.” The adoption extends the use of ACORD Solutions Group’s ADEPT technology in Bermuda, with Canopius Reinsurance Limited planning to incorporate additional brokers into the platform as part of its ongoing digital data exchange arrangements. Bringing data and query capabilities together on one platform supports more efficient processing of transactions and settlements in Bermuda and provides a scalable approach as we extend its use to additional brokers.” ACORD Solutions Group said the implementation represents another deployment of its technology within Bermuda’s insurance and reinsurance sector, where digital data exchange is being used to support the administration of accounting, claims and settlement activities.

item.title: Dutch Privacy Watchdog Advises Consumers Not to Purchase Smart Glasses
item.description: The Netherlands’ privacy watchdog AP on Thursday advised consumers not to purchase smart glasses, or AI-powered glasses with cameras, saying they are unsafe for both users and bystanders, after studying six types available on the Dutch market. Dutch consumer and rights groups sued Meta in October, alleging its glasses violate privacy laws, with a preliminary hearing scheduled for Nov. Also in October, Dutch retail chain Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium, in one of the first such moves by a retailer.

item.title: $3m financing backs launch of AI-enabled E&S MGA Alpine Specialty

item.title: Apis Partners takes minority stake in specialty MGA Alchemy Underwriting
item.description: Apis Partners has agreed to make a minority investment in Alchemy Underwriting, a London-based specialty insurance MGA, through its Apis Global Growth Fund III. Andrew Wallas, Chairman of Alchemy Underwriting, said: "We have experienced a strong sense of alignment, collaboration and partnership with Apis and look forward to growing the business as partners." item.title: Adam Riese takes over Neodigital portfolio

item.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
item.description: Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq tomorrow with a growth story that’s unlike any I’ve seen in close to three decades working in Silicon Valley: The company says revenue reached $17 billion in Q3, less than four years after Claude launched with zero. The San Francisco-based company also presents a stark contrast to the more common theme in recent years of venture-backed companies staying private longer: Anthropic is less than six years old as it goes public in a potentially record-setting listing. Those metrics are impressive, but there are other numbers in its S-1 I keep circling, too, like the nearly $900 billion in compute purchase and lease commitments.

item.title: Anthropic Prices IPO Shares At $83, Above Range
item.description: Anthropic priced shares for its upcoming stock market debut at $83 on Wednesday afternoon, solidly above the expected range of $70 to $78 laid out in its IPO filing, CNBC, Reuters and the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. For the IPO portion of its fundraise, Anthropic plans to sell just over 800 million shares, bringing in about $66.4 billion. The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

item.title: Morningstar DBRS calls for federal insurance backstop to strengthen Canada’s quake resilience
item.description: A government-supported insurance backstop would strengthen financial resilience and help support the stability of credit ratings.” According to Morningstar DBRS, introducing a federal insurance backstop could provide an additional layer of financial protection against extreme earthquake losses, complementing insurers’ existing capital and risk management arrangements. Morningstar DBRS, a global credit rating agency, has raised concerns over the potential impact of a severe earthquake on Canada’s insurance market, identifying federal government involvement in catastrophe insurance as a possible means of limiting financial losses and protecting the sector from widespread disruption. Morningstar DBRS explained that the country’s existing approach depends largely on commercial insurance arrangements and the Disaster Financial Assistance Arrangements (DFAA) programme, through which the federal government supports provincial and territorial disaster recovery efforts.

item.title: Cal-Maine Foods Shuts Production at Florida Facility Due to Bird Flu
item.description: Cal-Maine Foods said on Wednesday it would cull about 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its Florida facilities, forcing the US egg producer to temporarily halt production at the site. The company said it has suspended production at the facility while following US Department of Agriculture protocols, and will cull 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing 2.7% of its flock. The highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly called bird flu, has led to the culling of hundreds of millions of birds over the past few years, disrupting food supplies and driving up prices, though human infections remain rare.

item.title: Florida Mayor Declares Emergency as More Flooding Expected on East Coast
item.description: The mayor of Hollywood, Florida, declared a state of emergency as southeast parts of the state endured a new round of flooding after more than a foot of rain fell in just a few hours. “As low pressure develops and strengthens near the coast, winds from the east and northeast will increase.” The flooding in southeast Florida this week followed a previous round of unusually heavy rains, with floodwaters so high that it forced the temporary closure of a 90-bed rehabilitation hospital in Melbourne, Florida, last week, and flooded a number of homes and businesses. And more trouble may be on the way for the Southeast: AccuWeather meteorologists warned that the tropical system that triggered much of the deluge this week could bring more heavy rains and flooding to Florida and the Carolinas, and then into New York and New England by early next.

item.title: Strike Risk Grows at Busiest US Ports as Contract Talks Stall
item.description: Contract negotiations between security workers at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach and their employers have stalled, setting up a “real potential” for a strike starting on Saturday that could impact operations, according to the group representing terminal operators and ocean carriers. Related: Employers, Watchmen at California Ports Extend Contract Talks The previous labor contract expired in July 2025, and the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service has been assisting with negotiations between the ILWU’s Local 26, which represents about 250 security workers, and the employers. on Saturday, November 21, setting up the real potential for a strike at the nation’s busiest port complex,” PMA said Wednesday.

item.title: Why Insurers' Internal Software Builds Never Finish
item.description: Internal software builds at insurers routinely stretch past two years and $30 million because of a structural misunderstanding. This year I spoke with several people in insurance and insurtech whose internal software builds started in 2025. It found that purchased tools and partnerships succeeded about 67% of the time, and internal builds succeeded one-third as often.

item.title: The Claim Runs on the Data Captured First
item.description: The capture from the first visit has become the foundation the rest of the claim is built on, and increasingly the foundation that automation and artificial intelligence are built on, too. It is whether the capture produced data the rest of the claim can actually use. If it was not captured on the first visit, it is gone for good.

item.title: Allianz Life-backed Transparency Analytics discloses $3.4 million raise
item.description: Transparency Analytics , a New York-based credit ratings and analytics company backed by Allianz Life Ventures, reported selling $3.42 million in equity to five investors in a November 16 SEC filing. Allianz Life Ventures participated in the company’s December 2025 round, which was led by Deciens Capital and also included Mouro Capital, FJ Labs, SUM Ventures and Core Innovation Capital. Transparency Analytics assesses the creditworthiness of corporate borrowers and offers an automated portal that generates a preliminary rating based on the proposed terms of a debt instrument.
